subject: Priority lane surcharge & renewal credit structure
messages:
From: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@summitanalytics.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@summitanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SLA needs for pilot + renewal questions

Diego / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the latency profile looks promising. We are preparing a 6–12 month pilot and need pricing for a priority lane that guarantees 99.99% uptime and 100ms P95 for inference calls (burst tolerant). Two procurement questions: 1) can you provide a surcharge schedule for the priority lane vs standard routing, and 2) what renewal credit or uplift discounts are available if we commit to a 12‑month annual spend at the end of the pilot?

We also want 24/7 escalation coverage with an on‑call rotation and a named escalation contact. If you can send a short quote and an example escalation SLA (hours, response windows, retainer), that would be helpful — procurement will review next week.

Best,
Rebecca Lin
Head of ML Engineering
Summit Analytics

Attachment: example_arch_diagram.svg (image stub)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@summitanalytics.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, procurement@summitanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA needs for pilot + renewal questions

Hi Rebecca — great to talk earlier. Appreciate the clarity on the pilot scope.

Quick answers up front:
- Priority lane surcharge: we price priority lanes as an uplift on top of base consumption; for the pilot size you described I’m attaching a draft pricing worksheet with three tiers (Priority Lite, Priority Standard, Priority Plus) and incremental surcharges (10% / 18% / 30%).
- Renewal credits: we commonly offer a renewal credit that phases in based on commitment level at renewal; for a 12‑month commit after the pilot we can propose a 7.5% credit applied to the first renewal invoice, or an alternative flat discount structure tied to committed monthly spend.
- Escalation coverage: we can provide 24/7 oncall with a named escalation owner + 1 hour P1 response for Priority Plus; Priority Standard gets 4 hour P1 response with 24/7 paging. Details in the attached SLA stub.

Would you prefer the renewal incentive as a percentage credit or an upfront committed discount on the annual invoice? I’ll loop in our pricing team if you want an approved concession.

I’m copying Diego and procurement for visibility. Attached: Summit-SLA-Quote-v1.pdf, priority-lane-pricing-breakdown.xlsx (numbers are draft).

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: Summit-SLA-Quote-v1.pdf (pdf stub)
Attachment: priority-lane-pricing-breakdown.xlsx (xlsx stub)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: SLA needs for pilot + renewal questions — concession ask

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Rebecca's ask. Summit is a mid‑enterprise buyer, likely to convert to a $250k–$400k ARR account if pilot converts. They want: 99.99% uptime, P95 ~100ms, 24/7 escalation, and a renewal incentive for a 12‑month commit after pilot. My proposed structure (see worksheet):
- Pilot pricing: base + Priority Standard (18% uplift).
- If they sign committed 12m at renewal, we offer a 7.5% renewal credit OR an equivalent 5% upfront committed discount on the first annual invoice.
- We need to confirm whether we can absorb priority surcharge down to 15% for a smaller concession and keep Renewal credit at 7.5%.

Also: they asked for named oncall owner and a 1‑hour P1 option for Priority Plus (higher surcharge). If we want to keep margins, I'd prefer to offer Priority Plus only with a $12k/mo retainer for the dedicated oncall coverage instead of lowering the surcharge.

Can you advise approval on: (A) lowering priority surcharge to 15% for Priority Standard, and (B) approval for a 7.5% renewal credit OR 5% upfront discount? I can present either to the customer.

Thanks — happy to sync quick.
Connor
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: SLA needs for pilot + renewal questions — concession ask

Connor — sounds reasonable. Approve the following:
1) Priority Standard surcharge floor at 15% (one‑time concession for pilot to accelerate conversion).
2) Renewal credit: approve 7.5% applied to the first renewal invoice; keep the 5% upfront discount as an alternative only if they insist on immediate ARR recognition (we prefer the credit).
3) For 1‑hour P1 named oncall we should charge the $12k/mo retainer; do not reduce surcharge further if they take that option.

Please make the offer explicit in writing and include the retainer schedule. If procurement pushes for deeper concession, escalate to me.

—Ben
VP, Revenue Operations
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Rebecca — thank you for the patience while we reviewed internally. Below is a concise offer for the pilot + renewal path: 

Offer summary (Pilot → 12m renewal):
- Pilot routing: Priority Standard (15% surcharge on base inference consumption) — this is a time‑limited concession for pilot conversion.
- Escalation: 24/7 paging with 4 hour P1 SLA included in the surcharge. Optional Priority Plus (1‑hour P1 named oncall) available for an additional $12,000/month retainer.
- Renewal incentive: 7.5% credit applied to the first renewal invoice after a signed 12‑month commit at renewal. Alternative: 5% upfront discount on the first annual invoice if Summit prefers immediate discounting.
- Attachments: updated quote (Summit‑SLA‑Quote‑v1.pdf) and a pricing worksheet with the 15% surcharge baked in (priority-lane-pricing-breakdown.xlsx).

Next steps: if this aligns, I can (1) issue a revised quote and (2) generate a DocuSign envelope for the pilot statement of work + optional retainer addendum. If procurement would like to see a short example runbook for escalation handling, I can attach that as well.

Would you like the renewal credit or the upfront discount as the primary path?
